上周，在 Epic 举报了一名玩家在语音聊天中发出的威胁后，FBI 逮捕了该名 堡垒之夜 玩家。

Epic 举报了来自阿拉巴马州的资深 堡垒之夜 玩家 Edward Frith，原因是他在游玩 堡垒之夜 时发布了令人不安的信息。随后，FBI 找上门将其逮捕。
根据宣誓书（据 Aftermath 报道），使用用户名“WagesOfNinja”的 Frith 表示，他正在宣泄愤怒，因为他“真的想杀人”，并且“每天”都在考虑杀人。
“让我们看看 FBI 会不会找上门来，因为我也会把那些混蛋给毙了，”Frith 在 FBI 真的出现在他家门口之前说道。Frith 的其他言论同样令人不安，这位 堡垒之夜 玩家暗示他计划通过冲向警察来结束自己的生命。
Epic 就这些言论向 FBI 国家威胁行动部门 (NTOS) 的紧急威胁研究与分析危机小组 (EXTRACT) 进行了所谓的“自愿紧急披露”。随后，开发商向 FBI 提供了威胁言论的录音和文字记录。
这名阿拉巴马州居民于 9 月 23 日因违反跨州威胁通信罪被起诉。在 9 月 24 日提出“无罪”抗辩后，他被还押候审。
Epic Games 于 2023 年 11 月为 堡垒之夜 发布了全新的语音举报系统。该系统允许玩家在发现其他玩家违反社区规则时截取音频并进行匿名举报。
Epic 当时表示：“Epic 收到音频剪辑副本的唯一途径是开启语音举报功能，并且参与者主动使用游戏内的语音举报功能对语音聊天进行举报。”
一旦被举报，系统会抓取最后五分钟的通信内容，音频文件将发送给 Epic 的审核团队进行审查。根据通信内容的严重程度，玩家可能会面临封禁，或者像本案一样被移交联邦调查局。
同样，堡垒之夜 玩家也可以举报文字聊天，这些记录会保存 30 天。堡垒之夜 开发商还使用自动系统来检测有害语言，例如“自残、危害儿童以及现实世界的暴力威胁”。

图个好回忆：没有Steam和B站的年代，20年前的老玩家靠什么把游戏打通关？

content.v: https://i.17173cdn.com/2fhnvk/YWxqaGBf/cms3/VNqskgbuehuzpBy.gif!a-3-854x.gif
大家好，我是阅图无数的正惊小弟。
梗图登场，欢乐万两；会心一笑，回忆拉满！
游戏圈不乏让人值得铭记的历史，那么有没有那么一张图，它的出现会勾起你当年的回忆呢？
话不多说，今日回忆杀启动！
https://i.17173cdn.com/2fhnvk/YWxqaGBf/cms3/gThJtibuehuAlEk.png!a-3-854x.png
对于现在的玩家来说，想玩个新游戏，怎么弄？
Steam打开，搜索，点购买，下载，开玩。
卡关了？
攻略一搜一大把，博主精心制作的视频，恨不得手把手教你到通关，连藏得最深的彩蛋都给扒得底朝天。
https://i.17173cdn.com/2fhnvk/YWxqaGBf/cms3/vDthCUbuehuyFzF.png!a-3-854x.png
但往回倒二十多年，这一切可全是天方夜谭了。
没有宽带，没有直播，更没有铺天盖地的测评跟攻略。那个信息闭塞年代，多人第一次知道一款游戏叫什么、长什么样、怎么通关……
唯一的渠道，是报刊亭里一本薄薄的杂志。
https://i.17173cdn.com/2fhnvk/YWxqaGBf/cms3/EoVSfTbuehuAhzx.png!a-3-854x.png
说到中国的游戏杂志，老玩家脑子里蹦出来的，一定会有很多名字，像什么《大众软件》、《电子游戏软件》、《游戏机实用技术》……
当然，还有今天咱们要回忆的主角，被读者亲切称呼为“家游”的《家用电脑与游戏机》。
https://i.17173cdn.com/2fhnvk/YWxqaGBf/cms3/hzKQdnbuehuAgsn.png!a-3-854x.png
回忆一：最早的游戏杂志，让你 学电脑 的？
聊家游之前，得先聊一个人，孙百英。
1985年，29岁的孙百英还在《家用电器》杂志社当编辑。这人打小就觉得自己玩得少，对玩具格外上心，索性在杂志上开了个栏目，叫娱乐器具，专门聊时下新潮的玩具。
这栏目开着开着，就开出了点别的味道。
雅达利2600这种插卡游戏机进了版面，《家用电器》成了国内最早介绍电子游戏的期刊。
https://i.17173cdn.com/2fhnvk/YWxqaGBf/cms3/oentKmbuehuAgoy.png!a-3-854x.png
平时接触得多了，孙百英那点儿”玩心“就慢慢活泛了，电子游戏这东西，在中国有搞头。
娱乐器具一步步演变成游戏机连载专栏，后来还增加了电视游戏乐园、攻关秘诀两个栏目，也是饱受读者的好评。
这让他动了心思，决定自立门户，干脆办一本专业的游戏杂志。
https://i.17173cdn.com/2fhnvk/YWxqaGBf/cms3/RrjMpobuehuyFyA.png!a-3-854x.png
但那个年代要办个游戏杂志，可不是什么简单的事情。
当时的家用电脑还是稀罕物，电子游戏更是被不少人视为洪水猛兽，想光明正大地搞个专门介绍游戏的杂志，就四个大字——基本没戏！
孙百英前前后后折腾了一年多，光是书面的申请就提报了两次，走过的流程更是数不胜数。最后拉上北京裕兴机械电子研究所合作，以“普及家用电脑知识、寓教于乐”的名义向国家科委申报，才获得了刊号。
1994年6月，《家用电脑与游戏机》在北京西绦胡同一处地下室里创刊。
https://i.17173cdn.com/2fhnvk/YWxqaGBf/cms3/SvAIcCbuehuAfFC.png!a-3-854x.png
虽然家游这名字土得掉渣，却是大有讲究的。
“家用电脑”这四个大字顶在前头，缩在后面“游戏机”就不那么扎眼了。
家长看见游戏两个字，眉头先皱一半，可要是封面印着家用电脑，又会觉得：嗯，学电脑，好事。再往下翻，游戏内容藏在里面，小孩看得两眼放光。
就这样，一本杂志，两头都哄住了。
https://i.17173cdn.com/2fhnvk/YWxqaGBf/cms3/frTknhbuehuAhca.png!a-3-854x.png
杂志的基调也就此定下，主打一个科普为主、游戏为辅。
后面又添了句口号，叫电子游戏是通往电脑世界的捷径，更是让家长掏钱买杂志，心里都踏实了一些。
https://i.17173cdn.com/2fhnvk/YWxqaGBf/cms3/nRfaSPbuehuAgiC.png!a-3-854x.png
回忆二：群雄逐鹿，游戏杂志最辉煌的年代
聊到这，小弟得插一句题外话，家游既不是中国第一本游戏刊物，也不是最后一本。
往前数，1991年，福州有个叫傅瓒的业内大佬，写了本《电视游戏一点通》。游戏机介绍、游戏攻略、秘技、剧情，一应俱全。发售就卖爆，一年内五次再版，总印量冲过23万册，正式开创了中国游戏出版的先河。
https://i.17173cdn.com/2fhnvk/YWxqaGBf/cms3/SOFRIzbuehuAloe.png!a-3-854x.png
同一时期，上海有个开街机厅的老板，叫谭启仁。
他天天看大部分玩家投币进去，没几分钟就GameOver，玩不长久。在心疼之余动了“骗币”的心思，让玩家多玩会儿，自己也能多赚点。
于是，谭启仁跟几个街机高手合伙，编了本《电子游戏指南》，把当时常见的攻略和秘技全收了进去。
https://i.17173cdn.com/2fhnvk/YWxqaGBf/cms3/WwIoUvbuehuAmmC.png!a-3-854x.png
后来这本《电子游戏指南》跟《电子世界》联手，由电子工业出版社发行，以丛书的形式出了《电玩迷》。
可惜的是，《电玩迷》没能拿到正式刊号，丛书的形式又跟不上游戏更迭的速度又太快了，就成了转瞬而过的流星。
1993年，北京一家动画公司转型做游戏，顺带办了这本杂志给自己宣传，起名叫《GAME集中营》。
集中营这仨字，放在现在看倒没啥，可放在二十多年前就太扎眼了，搞得销量很是凄惨，只做了两期就换了马甲。
1994年，正式更名《电子游戏软件》，也就是很多主机老玩家心中的耶路撒冷——电软！
从FC、SFC，到后来的PS、土星SS，从《魂斗罗》《超级玛丽》，到《拳皇》《最终幻想》……可以说，电软是很多人梦开始的地方，梦里有搓了千百遍的连招，有水下八关的传说，还有各种真真假假的隐藏彩蛋。

这里还有个趣事，国内最早的主机大战，就是由家游跟电软发起的。
当时，电软刊登了一篇MD与SFC的机能对比，偏向MD的性能，被SFC派的家游编辑们逮着一顿喷，逮着就是一通输出，两边读者也跟着下场，吵得好不热闹。

items.title: Bit Reactor CEO Welcomes Return of Some Furloughed Staff for 'Continued Support' of Star Wars Zero Company
items.summary: Bit Reactor, the developer of Star Wars Zero Company, has begun returning some of its staff to the team after

others.title: Star Wars Zero Company Developer Sees Portion Of Furloughed Workers Return

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/13/zerocompanythumb-1786638152676.png
Bit Reactor, the developer of Star Wars Zero Company, has begun returning some of its staff to the team after furloughing an estimated 80% of employees just before the game’s launch.
Bit Reactor’s CEO Greg Foertsch revealed the news in a public post on October 7, where he explained that the furloughs were necessary to “help us eventually bring as many people back as possible.”

Foertsh said that bringing these staff members back to Bit Reactor was an “important step forward” in the studio’s “continued support for Zero Company,” and that the team looks forward to sharing more updates about the game “soon.”

“Having to ask team members to step away after we navigated unexpected business developments outside of our control and so close to launch was an incredibly difficult decision,” Foertsh wrote. “...This team means a tremendous amount to me, and I am incredibly proud of what we have accomplished together. Thank you to our fans for the incredible response to the game and for supporting us along this journey.”

Sources with information about the situation told GameFile that the number of Bit Reactor’s payrolled staff now account for “more than half of what it had been ahead of the furloughs,” meaning that there is still a sizeable chunk of furloughed staff who aren’t getting paid.

Star Wars Zero Company launched in August 2026 to rave reviews, getting a sparkling nine out of 10 from our reviewers here at IGN who praised it for being an “excellent tactical game that does a fantastic job of slathering on the same cinematic look and feel we saw in Respawn's Star Wars Jedi games, incorporating strong characters and a storyline that's refreshingly centered on non-Force users and a non-traditional villain.”

Despite its success, much of Bit Reactor’s staff were placed on leave without pay just before Zero Company launched, with reports indicating around 80% of employees were affected. This has become a recurring trend within the game development industry, to the point where Gears of War: E-Day developers were overcome with worry that they would get laid off after “crunching hard” to get the game out on time.

This is the latest news to get revealed about Zero Company after GameFile uncovered legal documents revealing that the game was initially pitched as a title within the Titanfall universe , with specific connections to Apex Legends . While this pitch ultimately didn’t go through, it’s certainly intriguing enough to make us wonder what such a game would have looked like, had it actually been made.

items.title: Blizzard promises to make the blue elves in World of Warcraft: Forever look worse (positive)
items.summary: Blizzard gave us the first images of how Skyborne will look in November.

content.v: A tension that will never go away as long as World of Warcraft: Forever exists is how true it is to the 2004 MMO. Blizzard signed up for this by creating an MMO that is trying to blend the old with the new so that anyone, regardless of their experience with WoW, can get into it.

That tension has been at its highest concentration with the new blue elves it debuted with WoW: Forever. The Skyborne have never existed in WoW before; they look almost exactly like the Blood Elves from The Burning Crusade expansion, but their lore tells us they're a faction of High Elves.

Some players love the twist on a race they've been asking to play for years, while others believe they tarnish the authenticity of an MMO that's trying to recreate the joys of playing the oldest era of the MMO. Even though the debate over the Skyborne will probably never be resolved, most players agreed that, at the very least, they looked way too new alongside WoW's crunchy old player models.

Blizzard said it would respond to the feedback about the Skyborne visuals before WoW: Forever launches in November and today it has done just that in a blog post promising to give them a retro makeover.

"Over the course of development, we have been aligning on the right range of fidelity and what feels like it belongs in the WoW: Forever world and what does not," Blizzard writes. "The team has learned much in the process, and that will continue to strengthen more with future content."
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/Kte2G9vDUDyzvCHhE54Poe-1920-80.png

Blizzard says the Skyborne "didn't quite meet the consistency and cohesion we are aiming for," and will be tweaking how they look with the "HD" player models setting on. There's an example of their druid forms in the post and you can see how the feathers and fur have harsher lines and shapes that fit much better with WoW's original style. The old version used to look extremely smooth with a bright light blue gradient covering their bodies and now everything is much more muted.

The people who play with the "SD" models on to fully live like it's 2004 will also get visually updated Skyborne, but they won't come until early next year. Blizzard's work-in-progress image shows a bunch of elves who have had their smooth features replaced with jagged, low-poly shapes. They're basically Skyborne on low settings and I think they look great. Blizzard says they'll have another update on the models—and their SD druid forms—when they're closer to being finished.

I wasn't convinced Blizzard would be willing to technically downgrade a race that costs $30 to unlock, but I'm glad it did. It sets a precedent for how close it wants the newest stuff in WoW: Forever to adhere to the classic MMO, and, hey, maybe it'll convince some people to chill out and see how things go when it's out of beta on November 4.

items.title: With Grand Theft Auto 6 poised to take over the world, I reached out to Jack Thompson and it did not go well
items.summary: GTA is mainstream now, but the fiery activist who raged against violent videogames in the early 2000s has not

content.v: https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/fXXhhLVg2y2Ut8Z6x6HzH6-1920-80.jpg

It's hard to imagine now, but a little over 20 years ago the gaming world was absolutely scandalized by Hot Coffee , a mod to activate abandoned code in Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas that enabled CJ to have interactive sex with his girlfriend.

The game was re-rated as "Adults Only" by the ESRB in 2005, forcing it off retail shelves—this was a time when retail shelf space mattered—and it was banned outright in Australia. Even the US Federal Trade Commission got involved, complaining that Rockstar and Take-Two Interactive "did not tell consumers that the game discs contained potentially viewable nude female characters and a potentially playable sex mini-game."
22 years later, with Grand Theft Auto 6 on the verge of console release, it all seems rather quaint. From the ESRB's newly posted rating , here's what we've got to look forward to in GTA 6:

All of which adds up to an M rating—that is, "generally suitable for ages 17 and up." PEGI, the European game rating agency, came down a little harder, rating it 18+ in a since-deleted listing that also noted the presence of "detailed decapitation" and "frequent and prominent" drug use.

How did we get from there to here? Well, we grew up—literally. The Entertainment Software Association said in 2025 that the average gamer in the US is 36 years old and has been playing for 18 years: That's police, politicians, and parents who all came up playing games (including GTA) and view them as no more remarkable than a spicy episode of Miami Vice.

The societal collapse that some alarmists anticipated, meanwhile, failed to materialize—well, it failed to materialize as a result of games, anyway. But a sudden uptick in violent crime and killings, sparked by "murder trainers" like GTA, Call of Duty, and Halo? It never happened. If anything, we've seen the opposite: As gaming has become increasingly mainstream, and the number of gamers has gone up, violent crime has seen a decline over the last two decades.

You could argue, I suppose, that the mainstreaming of Grand Theft Auto represents social desensitization—a loosening of the standards and decorum that made certain kinds of mature content much more taboo. But after years spent bearing witness to the moralizing hand-wringing that gave us the Satanic Panic , the Parents Music Resource Center , the bloody-minded determination to keep the Comics Code Authority alive despite its complete irrelevance, and of course the creation of the ESRB , I'm more inclined to think that what we're really doing is slowly figuring out what actually matters, and acting accordingly.
Plus ça change...

An infamous voice of criticism from this distant generation has not softened his position, however. With GTA now a mass-market entertainment franchise, no more frightening than a typical Marvel movie, I reached out to former attorney Jack Thompson; 20 years ago he was notorious among gamers for his determined, often theatrical efforts to link violent videogames to real-world violence and have them stringently regulated as a result, and I was curious how he felt about Florida's embrace of the GTA marketing machine , and the changed world we live in.

Thompson was such a high-profile presence on the videogame scene of the late 1990s and early 2000s that he was portrayed by Bill Paxton in The Gamechangers , a BBC Two docudrama about his long-running feud with Rockstar co-founder Sam Houser.

Thompson, who lives in Florida, is clearly unhappy with various GTA 6 promotional partnerships being enacted across the state. "If you don't understand that government promotion of commercial interests is fascism then we have very little to talk about," Thompson told me. "Ask the County Sheriff what she thinks about this unholy corporatist alliance."

I had in fact asked the sheriff , and the sheriff's department told me that it is not concerned by "promotional decisions [made] by private businesses or organizations." I relayed this to Thompson, who accused me of drinking the "fascist Kool-Aid," likened me to Joseph Goebbels, and told me to stop bothering him. He elaborated on that, very slightly, in a subsequent email: "The problem is your work proves you are not an honest journalist."

I feel a bit bad about that. I thought that with nearly 20 years of water under the bridge, Thompson may have softened, or at least reached a place where he could reflect soberly on the way the world has changed. That clearly hasn't happened.

Maybe that's understandable, because—and this isn't meant to be triumphal, I'm not spiking the ball, it's simple fact—after a life and career spent warring against it, Grand Theft Auto won. Netflix airs its special , the NBA wears its uniform , Walmart sells it, middle-aged cops and politicos buy it, and the state of Florida wraps itself in it. And here we are—we're fine. To me, that's a good outcome, but to someone who bet everything on the irresistibly corrosive impact of GTA? The absence of chaos and catastrophe—that everything is fine, at least in the sense that violent videogames didn't herald the end times—might just be a little disappointing.

content.v: 《GTA6》NPC可能主动攻击玩家。R星负责人Rob Nelson介绍，新作中NPC各有行动动机，玩家遭遇他们时，情况可能比系列以往更难预测。
街上路人会对你的行为做出动态反应：如果你尾随他人、凑上去偷听别人谈话、行为举止怪异，路人会做出对应反馈。同样的事件，会根据玩家的不同举动走向完全不同的结果。本作力量博弈机制深度升级，你不再是世界里的绝对强势者。部分路人会随身携带隐蔽武器，看到你作案会出手制止，也可能毫无征兆地和其他NPC爆发冲突。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261008/1791411199_830292.jpg
Nelson说在过去系列作品中，玩家在游戏世界里近乎“全能”，其他人通常会逃跑。新作还加入名为“犯罪档案”的系统。与《荒野大镖客2》荣誉系统不同，它并不简单地判定行为对错；如果玩家持续做出超出必要程度的行为，档案可能朝某一方向变化。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261008/1791411201_185322.jpg
杰森和露西亚各有日常行程。玩家切换角色时，另一人可能待在安全屋，也可能外出活动。Nelson举例说，当从露西亚切换到杰森时，有可能撞见杰森正在淋浴、全身赤裸。还有个支线任务，露西亚会遇到住在垃圾桶里的律师，她甚至可以直接跳进垃圾桶和对方互动。
杰森与露西亚拥有独立AI人格。两人一同在城中游荡时，其中一人会主动提议去做某件事，甚至会自己擅自跑开开启行动。他们是具备自主行为逻辑的独立个体。有玩家担心，要维系两位主角的人物关系会不会变得枯燥，只想体验爽快动作内容。Nelson回应，开发团队花大量功夫打磨两人之间的化学反应，同时保证他们也可以独立行动，两个角色无论是独处还是结伴都有出色表现。
Nelson还表示，金钱在本作故事中比以往更重要，玩家可能需要卖车或抢劫商店来筹钱推进任务。此外，饮食会影响健康，健身可以提升肌肉和力量，过量进食则会增加体重。

items.title: 'You have HOW MANY unread emails?' PC Gamer shares their inbox shame
items.summary: Think you can beat our totals?

content.v: Between midnight and 8:00 am this morning I received 56 emails. By the end of today that number will be well over a hundred, by the end of October I'll have about 4,000 more, and my total for 2026 will be in the neighborhood of 50,000 (work and personal combined.)

Fifty. Thousand. Emails. In a year! That's with (and I just counted) the 284 email filters I've set up to keep out at least some of the garbage, nearly 200 blocked addresses, and our publisher's own hypervigilant email security system in place—which diverted 27 emails to spam today alone . That makes it incredibly difficult to stay on top of the actual useful emails we want to see when we open our inboxes.

Email has become a waking nightmare, so that ugly red number on your phone or desktop showing you how many unread emails you have? Despite my headline up there, it really shouldn't be a source of stress and shame. It's not your fault email turned out this way .

So let's air it out. All of us! This week I asked my coworkers how many unread emails they have, and you can see their answers (and explanations) below. We welcome you to try to top us in the comments.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/wC7aUjGb8pW4neHoNS25gF.png
UNREAD EMAILS: 780

Chris Livingston, Senior Editor "This total is actually good for me, the result of spending an obscene amount of time over the past few years(!!!) setting up filters and unsubscribing from mailing lists I never signed up for. If I'd asked this question a couple years ago it would be a number too big to comprehend. This is a victory, believe it or not."
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/XRZDZcf8JTFbGkVwfLBtAZ.png
UNREAD EMAILS: 4,854

Kara Phillips, Video Producer "The minute this number ticks over, like, 10, I'm not going to clear it out for a good while. Anything important I open right away, and deal with. There's just so much junk all the time, always, that I don't want to waste my time going through it. I've got places to go. People to see. Emails to not read when I get to those places. Life's too short to keep an eye on my inbox 24/7."
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/XU4BXGqFGNSnLvpWdVEAyC.png
UNREAD EMAILS: 38,523

Evan Lahti, Strategic Director "Help, I'm the longest-serving member of PC Gamer in the publication's history. I have emails with most figures from the last 20 years of gaming, including [reaches arm into bottomless inbox, grabs something at random] a 2012 email with Notch saying that he was looking forward to (but also nervous about) participating in a PAX panel I was moderating. In emails from 2010, we were still including our AOL Instant Messenger handles in our email signatures. Time is an entropic scourge."
"I am an embodied sack of anxiety and if my unread mail gets over 300 I may permanently transition to a different state of matter" — Lauren Morton, Lead SEO Editor

UNREAD EMAILS: 5,488

Sean Martin, Senior Guides Writer "The combo of endless notifications you get working for a corporation (i.e. emails I see but don't need to be read) plus a job that necessitates being on loads of different press lists, really does just breed a vast quantity of emails. https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/ySQKbsLZRDb9zwYMtJjPx7.png
UNREAD EMAILS: 18

Phil Savage, Global Editor-In-Chief "I use unread emails as a sort of unofficial to-do list, which means quickly clearing away the ones that are junk, and leaving the others in stasis until I'm ready to respond. https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/vnS6S3Yu6x4kxszYEkK3dG.png
UNREAD EMAILS: 760

Joshua Wolens, News Writer "The true number of unread emails—that is, emails I literally have not read—in my inbox is far higher, surely somewhere in the tens of thousands. Fortunately, I have a robust system: I mark everything as read when the unread count hits 1k. Almost time to do it again, looks like. Gets earlier and earlier every month."

content.v: CyberConnect2社长松山洋近日表示，支持PlayStation游戏发行向数字版转型。他认为，数字游戏对玩家更方便；减少实体光盘相关开支，也可能提高开发者的盈利能力。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261008/1791409066_211745_jpg_r.jpg
松山洋谈到，发行实体游戏需要向PlayStation或任天堂采购光盘，这会在运输和销售流程之外增加一笔成本。因此，他赞成减少对光盘的依赖。
游戏容量也是他提出的理由。松山洋以《GTA6》为例，认为这样的大型游戏难以轻松装入一张光盘，其他现代游戏也可能遇到类似问题。
https://img.3dmgame.com/uploads/images/news/20261008/1791409067_406084_jpg_r.jpg
PlayStation游戏向数字版转型仍存在争议，业界并非人人赞同这一方向。松山洋此次表达的是对数字发行便利性和成本的看法，并非PlayStation全面停止发行实体游戏的公告。

items.title: This Fanatical Deal Drops Marathon on PC to $19.39, Cheaper Than Steam's Autumn Sale

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2023/05/24/marathon-blogroll-02-1684962151922.jpg

Steam launched its Autumn Sale last week , and the PC-inclined know these seasonal sales are pretty much the best time of year to buy games. Sometimes, though, the gaming giant isn't offering the best possible price.

On Steam, Bungie’s latest live action release, Marathon, has dropped to $23.99 . However, digital game stores like Fanatical and GMG are also running fall sales, and it just so happens that the former has Marathon Steam codes for even cheaper, at $19.99 .

According to price trackers , that’s a lower price than the game has ever been on the U.S. side of Steam. Regardless of your feelings about the hardcore extraction shooter, it’s hard to argue with that being a good deal.
Marathon on PC Drops Under $20 at Fanatical

Fanatical is a UK-based e-commerce platform under the Fandom umbrella. It’s one of our go-to storefronts for digital game deals, so you can rest assured you’re paying for something legit. And yes, it’s a Steam code, not some wacky third-party launcher situation.

As for Marathon itself, well, the game’s been through a lot. The first couple of trailers picked up some buzz on social media, but a troubled alpha test and plagiarism allegations led to some delays . A little thing called Arc Raiders launched during that delay, creating even more competition in the multiplayer shooter space. Still, Marathon reworked some assets, and Bungie launched the game this past March.

While Marathon has faced challenges building a massive player base, the fans it does have are particularly dedicated. That dedication is likely owing to the shooter’s emphasis on hardcore gameplay and community, though the developers have recently outlined their plans to make the game more accessible with future updates, like a PVE mode .

I’ve put my fair share of time into the game and can attest to the difficulty allegations. There’s something addicting about that learning curve, though, especially with the loot and progression systems. At the end of the day, you get fresh Bungie gunplay in a disgustingly stylish world.

I think IGN’s Travis Northup said it best in his 9/10 review : “Marathon is unapproachable, unforgiving, offputtingly creepy, and has a playerbase of violent goblins who exist solely to bash your face in with a brick, and for all of these reasons it's become my favorite extraction shooter of all time.”
There Are a Ridiculous Amount of Gaming Deals Right Now

For whatever reason, we’re in prime deals season right now. Aside from Steam, Fanatical, and GMG, Amazon has a whole Prime Day sale going on right now, which obviously prompted competing sales from Best Buy and Walmart . We’ve been rounding up all of the best gaming deals , but it’s worth clicking around for anything on your wishlist.

《异形：隔离》中的异形会在空间站持续追踪主角。有限的物资主要用于干扰或暂时阻挡它，而遭遇情境和环境的变化让追逐难以预测。《生化危机7》的玛格丽特则在一段时期内无法被杀死；她难以预料的行动，以及虫群和身体变化，进一步强化了惊悚感。
另外三名敌人也各有追击方式：《小小梦魇2》的瘦长男会从电视中现身，并通过瞬移缩短距离；《恶灵附身》的劳拉在追逐段落中只能被暂时阻滞，火焰能为逃跑争取时间；《死亡空间》的猎人即使被切断肢体也会再生，玩家需要先与它拉开距离，之后才有机会彻底解决。

items.title: Bobby's back
items.summary: The former Activision Blizzard CEO has joined the board of directors at Skydance, the company formed by Paramo

content.v: Former Activision Blizzard CEO Bobby Kotick, who left the company and the videogame industry at the end of 2023 following its acquisition by Microsoft, is back in the game. Skydance, the company formed by Paramount's acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery, has added Kotick to its board, where he will serve as an independent director.
In a press release , Skydance credited Kotick for building Activision Blizzard "into one of those world's most successful videogame companies" during his 32 years as CEO.

"Bobby led a global entertainment company through three decades of sustained growth, and he brings real perspective on building enduring franchises and connecting with fans," Skydance CEO David Ellison said. "His record of pairing bold strategic moves with disciplined capital allocation is exactly the experience we need as we bring our businesses together."

Skydance now owns a frankly alarming number of media companies and brands , and yes, gaming is in the mix. While the announcement of the acquisition's closure on October 6 focused on film, streaming, television, and "a leading content portfolio that includes live sports, a deep programming library and expansive collection of iconic brands and franchises," it also includes Paramount Games—which was founded earlier in 2026 , basically by mashing up Skydance Interactive and Skydance New Media—and the far more storied Warner Bros Games. A Variety report says those two operations will be merged into a single entity.
Today, we are Skydance. One team with a shared ambition to entertain, inspire, and inform the world through extraordinary storytelling. https://t.co/hdAJCYt0wm https://t.co/Uoc99Y9srG October 6, 2026
Thus, the obvious question: Is Kotick there to take the reins of the company's newly reconstituted gaming division?

It's possible: Skydance heaped praise on the former Activision boss for his leadership and business acumen. "He showed a rare ability to anticipate shifts in how consumers engage with entertainment, investing in new platforms, new business models and new ways of reaching fans while keeping creative excellence at the center of the enterprise," the company said, adding that "his experience scaling a franchise-driven business, managing the complexity of a global public company and steering major industry transitions will serve Skydance well as it navigates an evolving media and entertainment landscape."

But his tenure was also controversial. In 2021, the company faced allegations of " unlawful harassment, discrimination, and retaliation ," and was the subject of a lawsuit filed by California's Department of Fair Employment and Housing. At the time, PC Gamer, interviewed three women who cooperated with that investigation, and who described an unprofessional workplace where bad behavior was excused.

The matter was ultimately settled in December 2023, shortly before Kotick's departure: Activision paid $54 million to the state to settle pay and promotion inequity claims, and set aside another $47 million to handle accusations of gender discrimination; the California Civil Rights Department (formerly the Department of Fair Employment and Housing) dropped its sexual harassment suit, stating in the settlement that "no court or any independent investigation" has substantiated allegations of "systemic or widespread sexual harassment at Activision Blizzard" or that Kotick acted improperly with regard to handling workplace misconduct.

Earlier in 2023, Activision Blizzard paid $35 million to settle an SEC complaint that it had violated rules for the protection of whistleblowers and failed to disclose information to investors. The terms of that settlement stated that the payment did not represent an admission of guilt.
Kotick has previously served on the boards of the Coca-Cola Company and the Los Angeles County Museum of Art, illustrating that ultimately, these moves are all about business.

items.title: Controversial Horror Series Ropes Me Back In With Silent Hill’s Original Composer And Lady Dimitrescu
items.summary: The Remothered games are true cult classics in the way that players find them either insufferable or inspired.

content.v: The Remothered games are true cult classics in the way that players find them either insufferable or inspired. As a lover of developer Stormind Games' antique perversions, but also a hater of its convoluted storytelling, I regretfully exist somewhere in between. But I know I won't be able to resist the new Remothered: Red Nun's Legacy when it launches later this month, since the horror game legends who helped make the Italian gothic game are way too good. Red Nun’s Legacy will feature legendary Silent Hill composer Akira Yamaoka, and its Red Nun enemy is voiced by Resident Evil alumna Maggie Robertson.

Remothered: Red Nun's Legacy latest trailer, which premiered today during the latest Horror Game Awards showcase , revels in the weathered stone buildings and marble fountain angels of the game's Sicilian setting. Stormind Games' developers are based in Sicily themselves, so recreating the decaying decadence of the island for Red Nun's Legacy was like trying to catch a dream right upon waking: You may never remember every detail, but you know the smells and feelings perfectly, because you lived through them.

A statement to press explains, "The Sicily that Stormind Games recreated in Remothered: Red Nun's Legacy is the Sicily the team has always lived, seen, breathed. This trailer is a visual journey through the real places, textures, colors, and cultural details that shaped the world of Red Nun's Legacy, stemming directly from the memories of those who developed it."

It looks as gorgeous and imposing as a ballet school built by Dario Argento. But so did the original 2018 Remothered game Tormented Fathers and its 2020 sequel Broken Porcelain, and I don't love them as much as I wanted to.

I'm getting invested because the darkened glamor of Red Nun's Legacy is enhanced by Yamaoka, whose industrial grooves are just as irrefutable as Mt. Etna's mouth leaking lava in the game's far distance. Plus, actor Maggie Robertson, whose take on the bad vampire mother Lady Dimitrescu made fans delirious for a nibble on the neck, will no doubt inspire the same frenzy with her Red Nun stalker.

With these artists' help, I think Remothered: Red Nun's Legacy could become a true classic--no "cult" necessary. It's out on consoles and PC on October 27, and it's coming to Nintendo Switch 2 on December 3.

items.title: Steam is about to start getting some of the best Japanese pixel art in gaming history
items.summary: It only took about 35 years for these PC-98 games to start being released in English.

content.v: Japan's NEC PC-98 series of personal computers, popular in the 1980s and 1990s, were home to hundreds of adventure games and visual novels with absolutely impeccable pixel art. It was a whole vibe— sometimes cute , sometimes incredibly detailed with a very limited color palette , and very (very) often pornographic. Very few of these games were ever officially released in English—the whole pornographic thing probably being a big reason why—but better late than never, right?

A fan translation group named WINE has released five English translations for PC-98 games in the last three years, including a pair of horror adventures called Dead of the Brain and Dead of the Brain 2. And the first one is now getting an official release on Steam juuuust in time for Halloween, with enhancements like autosaves and "optional quality-of-life improvements such as hover hints and hit boxes."

I've played a chunk of Dead of the Brain 2, and can't fully recommend them—they're pretty basic and a bit tedious as adventure games, and in schlocky horror B-movie fashion love to throw in some sexual violence—but damn do I love how these games look. There are some gnarly death scenes that aren't spoiled by this trailer.
I've got to share a few screenshots of Dead of the Brain 2, which doesn't have a Steam page yet but has even moodier art than the first game:
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/QLY5yYXao4QooUnam73wrR-1920-80.png
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/2pDpppGrtFH5BB9Zd9ErqR-1920-80.png
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/kQeeunSHJvvtUUnPGKbijR-1920-80.png
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/N3BKEfNWct7QNH5aZpkmvR-1920-80.png

https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/H3qSjzXtvqTQXCHuhgv4wR-1920-80.png

It's rare for fan translations to get an official stamp of approval, but this release of Dead of the Brain is part of a deal between one of the most prolific PC-98 studios of the '90s, FairyTale, and (* sigh* ) Fakku, a US-based manga publisher I'll let you Google yourself.

Fakku seemingly bought the publishing rights to FairyTale's entire catalog, potentially meaning dozens of PC-98 games coming to Steam in the future. Hopefully they'll all be translated by people, not AI, but partnering with WINE for Dead of the Brain is a promising first move. I'm at least looking forward to more people getting to appreciate this era of pixel art without having to go through the complex process of getting a PC-98 emulator up and running.
Anyway, if you use Bluesky, follow PC-98 Bot for more good pixels.

items.title: Nivalis Nights review: An avalanche of fascinating characters carrying a decent shop sim on their backs
items.summary: An avalanche of fascinating characters carrying an alright shop sim on their backs.

content.v: Nivalis Nights is overwhelming. Intentionally, I suspect, to give me the immersive experience of living in a hyper-capitalist megacity hellscape. It has no map because Nivalis is canonically unmappable, only a HUD compass where my 20+ active quest markers all scuttle over each other, nearly as crowded as the alleyways of its layered, neon city where hundreds of citizens amble between giant apartments and fusion food joints.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/rpYCLkJsLGh2M9ThcqE9Cm-1920-80.png

What is it? : A quest-heavy cyberpunk shop simulation in a city obsessed with debt. Release date : September 29, 2026 Expect to pay : $25 / £22 Developer : Ion Lands Publisher : 505 Games Reviewed on : Intel Core Ultra 7 265, RTX 5070 Ti, 32GB RAM Multiplayer : No Steam Deck : Unspecified Link : Steam

One of those joints is mine. Ramen Noir is a floundering noodle bar left to me by a friend named Thaddeus who flees the city for mysterious reasons, saddling me with its complementary insurmountable debt of 50,000 Lims.

Thaddeus also left me a greenhouse. A salty lad named Crabface bequeaths me a boat. Some lady named Ma Gomba wants me to grow her enoki mushrooms. Danny Danetti wants my opinion on his donut recipes. A sentient vacuum needs my help fleeing the human wife of his deceased former consciousness. CorpSec Agent Teleshko suggests, nay, demands that I expand my operation by buying additional businesses. Oh, right, and there's a serial killer at large who's taking out people with massive amounts of debt. You know, like me.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/6M4vJbGhKMG54zFqgrWGZc-1920-80.jpg

Folks, I am just trying to scrape out a profit serving chicken noodle soup and beer while I hoof it back and forth from the market buying nearly-expired ingredients on the cheap until I can afford to hire a general manager who will free me up to pursue even one of these quests.
My day in Nivalis looks like this:
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/TXaGhFN8maRxJ5pAhzM4cE.png
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/75W3x7QYzmENWQkjoG6jZK.png
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/S9pB7jrTF8VKA5ZxyjxKKR-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/m6fJsT8cnPS9vZZqGA6WCG.png
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/4qzNX6TnXEnWW84DiEjTAP.png
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/XUuPJv5dG4vNGTuTDn63x4-1920-80.jpg
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/GNSAQqBWMyEbnN7BWzth9Y.png
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/9nRkPniWX2tsYmHtfaRsGb.png
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/Anhyk8jYXWpPn7ZTYcXuXE-1920-80.jpg
Just a slice, please

Nivalis Nights calls itself a "slice-of-life" sim, which is a close enough description of what you get when you borrow life sim decorating, shop sim management, open-ish world exploration, farm sim produce production, and bungee cord them all together with a surprisingly story-heavy quest structure.
In the first five-ish hours, I worried that the genre soup of Nivalis Nights was going to ultimately disappoint me. Everything I found to praise about it came with a caveat.
Seems great
BUT
Exploration
The city is beautiful to look at and the layered, extremely vertical level design makes the possibility of exploring it seem fascinating.
There isn't much drive to explore aside from finding more silent vendors, sitting to eat similar meals at rival restaurants, and a scavenger hunt for broken fuse boxes.
Management
Shop management has some neat layers like customizing recipes with different ingredients and optimizing efficiency of kitchen layout and work shifts.
Babysitting my shops by actively participating feels a little dull with very repetitive customer appearances and awkward first-person cooking animations.
Decorating
Renovating restaurants with new cabinet styles or decorations seems like catnip for a build mode fiend like me, especially with free, non-grid placement.
Placing furniture and cabinets in first person without snapping to walls is actually really finicky and being strapped for cash means I don't really get to indulge in beautification.
Romance
Completing quests with certain characters can also lead to pursuing romances with them.
The payoff on the couple I've tried is a date with a shortish conversation and no further acknowledgement of being in a relationship.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/MSyfNXZ4CtvCRXfhCmfUsB-1920-80.png
It's a personality hire

What I found after several hours and a couple in-game weeks in Nivalis is that the characters are the star feature. I'll allow myself a heavy-handed food metaphor, given the context: The characters and setting are the eggs of Nivalis Nights. Whip 'em up with those dry ingredients and they become a leavening agent to make that batter rise, baby.

The streets of every district are jam packed with people. Many are unnamed, silent NPCs but a surprising number are fully voice-acted characters with stories and quests, some of whom can eventually work at my shops. Sometimes they don't seem immediately relevant until suddenly I'm five steps deep into someone else's quest and they ask me to find a specific hacker who, oh wait, I know that guy!
Their stories run a full neon spectrum from comedic corporate satire to strikingly earnest stories of people crushed beneath inherited debt:

Danny Danetti sells donuts in Meridian Market district near Ramen Noir and affably undermines the CorpSec demand that businesses always compete and never fraternize by checking up on me and trading recipe ideas.

Lois Gyo is a burnt out game designer for a major corp who initially comes off as a goofy shut-in but over time really grew on me as she strives to stay positive and develop friendships in a soul-crushing environment.

Pilk Dane is my piece-of-crap landlord, a bumbling dork just trying to make a buck off people below him despite having zero intimidation factor. Finding out his side hustle made me laugh, just not in the way he intended.

Sal Magundi II is a chef with augmented arms that are presently detached from his body and working in the kitchen while he's off walking around town bellowing orders to his cooks between talking to me.

Lochlainn McKenna has the face of a corpster but he's just the gentle dad to four kids he can barely afford, including the one with a respiratory condition exacerbated by living on the lower city levels and only treatable by prohibitively expensive equipment. I don't think I'd even have seen his story if I hadn't hired him to work at my third restaurant.

There are dozens more of them (At least 121, by count of the portraits in the "known characters" section of my menu) all with nuanced stories and genuinely excellent vocal performances that really sell some of the moments when they turn from goofy caricature to gut-spillingly relatable.

The amount of quests and story content that weaves these characters into each others' lives and into the main plot of a debt-chasing serial killer stalking the lower districts is a delight. I'd expected for the shop management and decorating to be the real draw in Nivalis Nights, but instead it's this vibrant, enormous cast of characters who are really motivating me to beat the streets every day, navigating labyrinthine districts in search of the next thread to pull.

Nivalis Nights is an alright shop sim with some okay decorating and a nod to life sim romances, but it's an excellent place . It's a smog-filled techno hellscape full of people with "generational debt" loomed over by advertisements about transferring the consciousness of your pet dog into any body, forced to live in nearly religious adherence to capitalism. I'd eat up a novel set here. Lacking that, I'll probably develop strong feelings on head-canons about its characters and spend hours tooling for new angles in its photo mode long past rinsing the simulation game this world is hiding in.

content.v: The Outlast Trials , Red Barrels' co-op horror game set in its wider Outlast universe, just broke its concurrent-player record, eclipsing 120,000 players. The previous high came when the game launched in Steam Early Access in 2023 and the player count climbed to 36,000.
Today's new record means the indie horror game reset the bar with a total more than four times higher than its previous best.

Red Barrels credited a few big factors for the record. For one, The Outlast Trials is enjoying a huge discount in the Steam Autumn Sale , on sale for $4--though that sale ends tomorrow (Thursday, October 8), if you're interested.

The studio also revealed that roughly half of the players contributing to that total are from China, as the game is seeing a surge in popularity there. Naturally, the Halloween season helps too, even though it's not one of the new horror games coming out this month .
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/image_abf886.png?w=636

The Outlast Trials made its version 1.0 debut in the spring of 2024. Though it's playable solo, it's intended to be experienced as a co-op game for up to four people. Seasonal content and events have come to the game regularly since then, adding new villains, abilities, maps, and more.
Up next for the game is its annual Geister event for Halloween, followed by Season 8 in December, which will add another new major villain, or "Prime Asset," as well as a new map and more events.

The Outlast Trials is a favorite on GameSpot, featured in our best horror multiplayer games list and our best horror games (overall) list. In my Outlast Trials review , I said it's "capable of being as terrifying as previous Outlast games, and though you’ll trade away some scares when playing with a bigger group, they’re likely to be replaced by nervous laughs as you and your allies narrowly evade monsters in the dark."

items.title: We tried to earn as much gold in WoW: Forever as we could in 2 hours—which involved a mugging, slander, and at least one crashout
items.summary: Wisdom, charisma, and courage.

content.v: If you want to make money in World of Warcraft, well… I cannot rightly say that we at PC Gamer are any good at it, based on the evidence given to us—but we are at least inventing new ways of money-making. And isn't invention the mother of necessity? Or was it the other way around? Who cares, we've got pockets to line.

I wrangled two of my erstwhile co-workers, Fraser Brown and Joshua Wolens, to see which of us was the best at making money in World of Warcraft: Forever's beta. Which felt like a fair testing ground, given both how populated it is and how un-inflated its new, fledgling economy would be. Here were the rules:

Each of us entered with a different strategy. Well, two of us did (more on that later) to try and make the most bank. I, the Orc of Wisdom, would weaponise my 15+ years of roleplay experience to trade knowledge with the masses. Josh, the Majestic Celebrity, would try to wield his status as a games journalist and very famous person to his benefit—hamstrung only by the fact he had never actually played much World of Warcraft.
There was also Fraser, as Boeuf Beef, who did a secret third thing. I'll let him enlighten you about his masterful machinations myself.

This is a story of wisdom, courage, and bull-headed bravery—and, more importantly, it's a story of how those virtues could be mercilessly weaponised to siphon as much money from the economy as possible.
I've been roleplaying in MMOs for about 16 years—it is, in fact, what got me into writing—so rather than simply beg the masses for hand-outs, I would use it. I am, first and foremost, an entertainer.

I assembled a document full of snippets of wisdom—some reworded adages and sayings, others my original work—and decided to leverage them around WoW: Forever's new campfire feature. For those not in the know, anyone with a cooking skill can set down a campfire, around which may be set various fixtures. Sit around the fire for a minute, and you'll get buffs.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/eBYMYYMsojYbhcxVu7dJoc-1920-80.png

This made for a pretty cheap initial investment of seven silver and 66 copper: Enough to train my cooking skill as well as some simple wood and tinder. All of which was available on the jog up to Razor Hill, which was very pretty. An auspicious sign, I thought, for my journey.

With the ability to make campfires in hand, I parked myself somewhere people would be forced to interact with me by game mechanics alone: The top of a zeppelin tower. Being the only convenient route to the Undercity, home to the new Ruins of Lordaeron dungeon everyone was keen to try, passengers would be forced to stand around while I gave them my spiel.

Originally, I was going to set a static price for my wisdom—but at the last minute, I decided to change my tact to simply requesting whatever people could spare. I am, after all, a humble old orc simply looking for a hot meal and a place to stay. Durotar nights get so very cold.

And, listen—I'm guilty of my fair share of cynicism of the MMO populace, but the two hours I spent up here were nothing short of delightful as the WoW community played ball. Here's a short-list of the characters I encountered:
I had a lovely old time—and one that was very profitable. My final score—minus my initial silver stipend—can be found at the bottom of this article.

I don't know what WoW is. I don't know what my abilities are. I don't know where this zeppelin is taking me and I don't know what the buttons in my hotbar do. I don't know what any of this shit is and I'm fucking scared .

What I do know: I'm incredibly important. My name is on something like 68 million articles on PC Gamer dot com, making me a rough hybrid of Scarlett Johansson and George Herbert Walker Bush in fame and significance. Play to your strengths, they always told me, so off I went to ignore circa 99% of WoW's actual mechanics in favour of simply impressing my incredible renown on other players and asking them for money.
My other strength is slander, so at the same time as I harangued people about my own importance, I also let them know that my two opponents were dreadful. Just utter bastards.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/V2Tew7FZ2Hp7P7GrdsAJ6D-1920-80.png

This worked alarmingly well. Did you know you can just ask people for money and get it? I might try this out in real life. Just a few minutes in, my very first beg netted me some silver pieces and well-wishes.

The issue was not the effectiveness of my tactics but my complete unfamiliarity with the videogame 'World of Warcraft'. I quickly realised that I had genuinely no idea what the relative value of these coins were . Is a silver piece nothing? Is it a billion dollars? Am I the richest man in MMO history already?

Likewise, simple mechanics hamstrung me. Did you know to actually get into The Undercity there's a whole elevator system? I didn't! So instead I just sort of roamed around the top part for a while, unsure what kind of zone I was even in. This was, on reflection, not a lucrative use of my time.

The highlights of my adventure? I'll be honest, I mostly just had a pleasant time ambling from town to town and asking people to give money to the world's most important man (me). This did backfire once, though.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/xTYArAPbLraeakyrb6a42a-1920-80.png

In dialogue with one player, Zippie Skadoo, I referred to him as a "good man" (or maybe "good friend," I forget). It turns out this was not acceptable. Zippie Skadoo quickly educated me that he was, in fact, bad to the bone, on the verge of going berserk, and might be inclined to assault me.
So that could have gone better.
Elsewise? I reckon I could have won this thing had I not wasted time in A) The Undercity and B) taking a boat or something to another continent and getting repeatedly killed by panthers for a bit.
Lessons for next time, I suppose, when Majestic Celebrity once again graces… Azeroth(?) with his presence.

I've been playing WoW off and on since 2004. So you'd think I'd find this challenge a doddle. Nope! This was, and I am not prone to exaggeration, the worst two hours of… if not my entire life, at least this month.

OK, so, I didn't have a plan. Or rather, my plan was to tell everyone I had an amazing plan, in the hope that an amazing plan would just pop into my brain. It did not. What actually happened was I rushed headfirst into insanity. It's a good thing the video accompanying this is short, because I really don't want the world to see the extent of my madness.
At one point, I just started making animal noises.

After failing to prepare a plan, I decided to simply skin a bunch of critters and make money that way. Perhaps selling them to generous players. Easy, right? Obviously not, or I'd still have my sanity. I have listened back to my full recording and plucked out some choice quotes.

So, yeah, I had a great fucking time . And then I had to listen to my two-hour descent into madness. Which, let me tell you, was not fun! I got to relive the experience of wasting time and money when I should have been making money.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/EBsdDhdbiAJMWnjYbPJ9e8-1920-80.png

At one point, I spent about 20 minutes trying to complete a single quest, which I should add only promised a reward of two silver. I never really dipped into WoW Classic, so I forgot how unforgiving OG WoW was. I'm not used to being a weak baby who will die as soon as a large bird or boisterous pig-man so much as looks at me. And I was already tired and annoyed by this point. I could have moved on. But I was determined to complete this stupid bloody quest. And I did it! I got my two silver.

items.title: World of Warcraft: Forever drops the PvP grind so normal people can have fancy titles too
items.summary: Blizzard outlines how PvP ranks will work in the throwback MMO.

content.v: Even though I was way too new (and low level) to understand how PvP worked in World of Warcraft's early days, I knew by osmosis that it was made for tryhards. WoW PvP was not only a massive grind, but a competition against other grinders for a unique title that no normal person would even dare to go for.

WoW: Forever borrows a lot from the classic game, but the torturous PvP system won't be one of them. In a new blog post , Blizzard explains how it has simplified the system overall to avoid asking players to derail their entire lives for bragging rights.

Those old titles are still there—High Warlord for Horde players and Grand Marshal for Alliance—but you won't be racing to keep your place on an invisible leaderboard every week. Instead, it's going to be pretty straight forward: Anyone who plays a lot of PvP will get rewarded eventually.

You'll have a currency and a point-based progression system to worry about. Honor is the currency you'll earn for killing enemy players, completing battlegrounds, and finishing PvP quests. Blizzard says it has normalized Honor gains across all the different battlegrounds so that none of them are more efficient than the others. As you do all of those things, you'll earn Rank points that unlock 14 tiers of rewards, which include powerful PvP gear and those flashy, prestigious titles. Rank points will have a weekly cap, too, so you can't just marathon to the end over a weekend.

All of this will be wrapped up in a PvP season that will reset once a new one starts, presumably to let Blizzard add a fresh set of rewards encouraging players to do the climb all over again. Every season will have weekly tasks that will give you bonus Honor and Rank points as well as a Legacy Point, Forever's account-wide meta progression system.

While I'm sure the most hardcore WoW veterans will scoff at the idea of normies running around with fancy PvP gear and titles, I don't think it would be responsible of Blizzard to ask people to stay up for multiple days trying to maintain their place on a leaderboard. Back in the old days, the system incentivized people to share their accounts with friends or guildmates just to keep up. The new system, while still a grind, follows Forever's general ethos of capturing the spirit of the old MMO while making it realistic for people who can't spend every waking moment of their lives logged in.

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/08/20/mw4-mp-1787240916718.jpg
A prominent Call of Duty esports commentator has opted to resign from his role after pursuing a romantic relationship with his co-commentator's ex-wife.

In what is one of the most unique stories of the week, Call of Duty League commentator Clint "Maven" Evans has announced that he's stepping away from the CDL for the "foreseeable future." He noted that this decision came after he chose to pursue a romantic relationship with the wife of his co-commentator, Joseph "MerK" DeLuca. Evans noted that he recognized that the situation is "taboo" and "unconventional" in a statement.

"As some of you know, I was very close to my casting partner Joe and his family," Evans wrote. "Maurisa was one of my best friends. We remained friends, after they divorced, and along the way it became more than that and we started dating. I understand how unconventional/taboo it is. It’s truly not something I ever foresaw happening."
He went on to note that he hopes to return to the CDL in the future, but has acknowledged that it may not happen.

"I hope that one day I’ll be back working on the CDL," he continued. "If not, it was a hell of a ride, and I appreciate the love over the years. Please continue to show support to Joe, the CDL, and its talent!"

Naturally, the Call of Duty e-sports community has had some very intense reactions to the news. Many feel that Evans betrayed his friend, whom he has known for well over a decade. DeLuca hasn't commented on the situation and hasn't posted on his X page since October 4. The start date for the upcoming CDL season has yet to be formally announced, but historically, it begins in December, shortly after the latest Call of Duty is released.

items.title: Skate has been de-live serviced by ReSkate, a modding platform downloaded 350,000 times—devs say they will comply if EA's lawyers come knocking
items.summary: ReSkate makes Skate playable offline, and enables custom servers and maps. It's been an instant hit.

content.v: What's going on?

EA's reboot of the Skate series is a free-to-play online game with mixed user reviews on Steam . Aspects of Skate are well-liked, but a common complaint is that it lacks the spirit of skate culture, exchanging grittiness for brand-name premium cosmetics and tidy-looking maps in an online-only ecosystem that prevents true DIY modding.

Enter ReSkate , a new "modding platform" created (with AI assistance) by a pair of coders who go by zee_x64 and ReGlitched. The modders have experience with other custom server projects, namely R5Reloaded , which allows free-to-play shooter Apex Legends to be modded and played privately.

In just a few days, ReSkate was downloaded from GitHub over 350,000 times. The software hooks into a particular version of Skate on Steam and allows it to be played offline, in custom servers, and with custom maps and other assets.
"Honestly didn't realize how big this was going to be," zee_x64 told PC Gamer over Discord this week. "We were just doing it for the love of the game."
We were just doing it for the love of the game.
zee_x64, ReSkate modder

The modders say they aren't trying to undermine Skate developer Full Circle or "replace the live game," and have no personal issues with Skate's microtransactions. "For me the game is free to play and they need to make money somehow to be able to keep developing the game," zee_x64 said.

To that end, ReSkate will only work with the current version of Skate and isn't being promoted as a way to get premium content for free. Mods that unlock premium cosmetics are disallowed, at least in ReSkate's official channels.

Still, ReSkate does allow us to download a free-to-play game and then break out of its walled ecosystem, adding our own cosmetics and custom maps, and playing it without the need for EA's servers and anticheat software, which also makes it playable on Linux via Valve's Proton emulation. (But does not make it possible to cheat in official servers, because ReSkate doesn't interact at all with EA's servers.)

Lawyers have sent letters over less, and if EA comes knocking with a cease and desist order, zee_x64 says they won't put up a fight. But ReSkate is open source, and there are already over 70 forks on GitHub , so it may not be something that can be put back in the box.
https://cdn.mos.cms.futurecdn.net/sfLMXAPYVfag9zRTCgGPhG-1920-80.png
The player response

On the unofficial Skate subreddit, players are posting videos of custom cosmetics and maps—Counter-Strike maps made it in immediately, of course—and debating what ReSkate's effect on the live game will be.

One person is excited simply to have the option to choose any shirt color for their avatar. "The fact I can just open up a modding tool app; design the material type; design the colour; and not wait for the devs to release a specific version and wait for it to release on rotation is just great," they wrote .

Others are less convinced that ReSkate is a boon, with some expressing sympathy for Skate's developers on the expectation that the platform will negatively affect the game's future. One popular comment speculates that EA could come to "see [Skate] as a failed experiment and shuffle resources elsewhere."
At the time of writing, EA has not commented publicly on ReSkate.
AI tools sped up development

Custom server projects for defunct MMOs and long-running live service games have been a thing for a long time, but they aren't typically released while a game is still in early access. A 2026 wrinkle in this particular case is that the modders say development was substantially accelerated by AI coding tools.

"We used AI to help reverse [engineer] the game as I don't see any reason not to when the tooling exists," zee_x64 said. "Without it, it probably would of taken years to do the same thing … that also doesn't mean we blindly just prompted AI until it worked, we still had to use our previous knowledge to get it actually working."
Antivirus flags complicate the install

A heads-up for potential ReSkate downloaders: Windows antivirus doesn't like it, and you may have to create an exception for the file to avoid it being quarantined, an uncomfortable step despite the modders' assurance that it is a false positive.

"Some antivirus software may flag ReSkate because it uses techniques that can resemble malware, such as DLL injection, process/memory modification, and downloading files over HTTPS," says kushWRA1TH, a mod in ReSkate's Discord server . "These are used for its game-mod functionality and do not by themselves mean ReSkate is malicious."
Even if ReSkate itself is not malicious, downloading and using it does carry a risk, as it could contain exploitable security flaws. (As can any software.)

The modders note as well that they cannot vouch for every fork of the code, referring to versions created by people other than the original modders. As an open source project , ReSkate's inner-workings are available for anyone to analyze or modify.

items.title: Resident Evil Movie Will Become Zach Cregger’s Biggest Ever, Surpassing Weapons
items.summary: Zach Cregger has another hit on his hands with Resident Evil, and it's set to become his biggest movie ever by

content.v: Zach Cregger has another hit on his hands with Resident Evil, and it's set to become his biggest movie ever by revenue at the box office.

According to Deadline , Resident Evil is expected to surpass his current biggest movie, Weapons ($270 million worldwide), by the end of this week or sooner. It currently stands at $247.6 million worldwide.

What's propelling Resident Evil higher was its release in China this week--it debuted there on October 5, and it's expected to make $35 million in China for its first week. If this comes to fruition, Resident Evil should pass $280 million globally this week.

The previous Resident Evil movies from director Paul W.S. Anderson also performed phenomenally in China. The last one, 2016's The Final Chapter, made $159.5 million in China alone, making up more than 51% of the movie's worldwide gross of $312.2 million. It's the highest-grossing Resident Evil movie ever. Cregger's Resident Evil still has work to do to catch up.
Cregger's earlier movie, 2022's Barbarian, made $46 million worldwide. Long before that, Cregger made Miss March, and it earned $4.6 million worldwide.
In terms of all video game movies, Resident Evil ranks No. 17 , but if it does indeed reach $280 million, it will pass 2018's Tomb Raider ($274.6 million worldwide).

Resident Evil is doing great commercially and scored solid reviews from critics, so people might expect a sequel. That could happen, but Cregger has said he's finished with franchise movies , even though he does have ideas for more stories .
Cregger's next movie is The Flood, a deep-space sci-fi movie starring Jennifer Lawrence. It has nothing to do with Halo , despite bearing a name with ties to Halo .

content.v: What likely would have been the big new enemy faction of the Halo universe, the Endless, have been fully revealed, though it's unclear what role, if any, they will play going forward.

As announced last month by Xbox's Matt Booty, Halo is under new management , with the responsibility of the next game in the series going to a completely new team under Activision. Halo Studios, formerly 343 Industries, will remain as a small team to oversee already-released titles like the recent Halo: Campaign Evolved. However, the majority of the studio, 268 people, have been laid off.

In the wake of the news, the latest (and now last) issue of the lore-focused Canon Fodder blog written by Halo Studios community writer Alex Wakeford has now become a parting gift from the studio to the community. In it, Wakeford reveals a glimpse at what the future of Halo might have looked like under Halo Studios' continued stewardship.
https://www.gamespot.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/XalanynEmergence.jpg?w=636

There are plenty of reveals within, including a look at Zeta Halo environments that may have at one time been planned for Halo Infinite DLC. But the biggest reveal is saved for last: an image that is the community's first full look at the Endless. This new enemy faction was teased in Halo Infinite via the Harbinger, a member of an advanced race that was imprisoned by the Forerunners on Zeta Halo due to their ability to survive the firing of the Halo rings.

In the blog the Endless are referred to as the Xalanyn, children of Abaddon. Wakeford doesn't elaborate further, but states that he hopes the image will "spark your imagination and let your canon curiosities run wild with endless questions."

Each member of the Endless looks wildly different. Some appear vaguely humanoid, while others look more like some type of sea creature. Every Endless member appears alongside a smaller creature that is reminiscent of their Endless counterpart. The Harbinger appears in the image alongside a Skimmer, a new enemy type encountered in Halo Infinite.

The image seems to point towards the Endless being almost a replacement of sorts for Halo's traditional Covenant faction, with each Endless supplying a smaller enemy type the Master Chief would have to battle against. Interestingly, an Engineer, an alien race used by the Covenant and seen in previous entries in the franchise, appears alongside a similar looking Endless in the image. This looks to imply the Engineers themselves were created or in some way linked to the Endless.

Unfortunately, this may be Halo fans' first, and last, look at the Endless. According to Halo insider Rebs Gaming , nobody at Halo Studios is currently involved in Activision's new Halo . Activision may completely disregard Halo Studios' work in favor of a clean slate , though Rebs does state Activision's game, while not a direct sequel to Halo Infinite, also won't "retcon any previously established canon."

Halo's move to Activision comes as Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has put a renewed emphasis on big franchises as part of her "Xbox reset" strategy that has seen widespread layoffs , game cancellations, and studio divestitures.

items.title: Gears of War E-Day Is a 'Natural Choice to Be an Exclusive' – Studio Head Mike Crump Claims Series Carries the Banner for Xbox
items.summary: Gears of War: E-Day launched this week, and while it is excellent, the game was pulled away from a PS5 launch

others.title: Xbox Game Pass Gets Gears Of War: E-Day And These 11 Games In October

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/01/gears-1790854472442.jpg

Gears of War: E-Day launched this week, and while it is excellent, the game was pulled away from a PS5 launch earlier this year. In a recent interview, The Coalition Studio Head Mike Crump claims that this was all part of the plan.

In an interview with the BBC , Crump defended the choice to be an Xbox exclusive, despite a likely ludicrous budget saying, "Gears has been an exclusive franchise to Xbox for 20 years now. It's sort of entwined deeply with the brand."

However, Gears of War: Reloaded did launch on PS5 last year, so the franchise as a whole isn't exactly Xbox-exclusive anymore. It's also likely that if E-Day did launch on PlayStation, it'd see higher sales numbers.

Crump claims that the metrics for success go further than that, though. He told the BBC that the series is meant to, at least in part, carry the banner for the Xbox platform and give people a "reason to be in the Xbox ecosystem." Queue Xbox CEO Asha Sharma's decision to pull the game from the PS5 release slate.

Regardless, the game will now likely have lower sales than it otherwise would have. When the BBC asked Crump about that, he insisted that the studio is taking a broader view than just looking at sales figures and retention numbers.

"We measure things like, are we showcasing the platform? Are we pushing the hardware to it limits? Are we showcasing what the Xbox is capable of? ...Our goal basically is to be the best-looking game on the Xbox and really show the industry what's possible with our hardware," he answered.

If the goal is to be a tech demo about what the Xbox consoles are capable of, I'd argue that it's a straight-up success. The game looks incredible on both the Xbox Series X and Series S, so much so that The Coalition had to rely on trickery with the Page File to get the game running smoothly on the less-powerful console. The game is also incredible, and our reviewer Ryan McCaffrey gave it a 9 , saying:

"By going back to the beginning, Gears of War: E-Day returns to the heart of this series: Marcus Fenix, Dom Santiago, and a Locust horde that’s as terrifying as it is dangerous. E-Day pulls off the tightrope act of giving us a heartfelt prequel with strong characters even when we know how it ends. On a more mechanical level, it also evolves the enemies, weapons, and combat you’d expect to deliver a Gears of War campaign that stands toe-to-toe with any of the others. It wraps up with 10 years still left to go before Marcus gets tossed in prison ahead of the events of the first Gears of War, so here’s hoping the next one stays in the past for a while longer – and that we don’t have to wait another seven years for it to arrive."

But even if the game is a critical hit and a technical marvel, sales numbers will inevitably play a role in the game's success, especially as Microsoft is currently in the middle of a months-long restructuring campaign. Right after launch, developers at The Coalition told Eurogamer they were expecting layoffs. However, Crump has since addressed those concerns , saying, "For us that's about shipping a great game that people are going to love and I feel like, as a team, we've done that."
Let's just hope that a pretty game and high review scores really are enough to keep the Xbox layoff machine at bay.

items.title: Capcom Clarifies Stance on AI After RE Engine Conference Comments
items.summary: Resident Evil and Street Fighter developer Capcom has clarified its stance on AI and its future plans for the

content.v: https://assets-prd.ignimgs.com/2026/10/07/capcom-clarifies-stance-on-ai-1791395067864.jpg
Resident Evil and Street Fighter developer Capcom has clarified its stance on AI and its future plans for the RE Engine in an exclusive conversation with IGN.

Capcom held its yearly recruitment conference on October 2, wherein programmer Satoshi Ishida outlined the company’s plans to incrementally improve its RE Engine using a program called REX (short for RE Next Engine).

Rather than building a new engine from scrap, Ishida explained that a series of steps will be taken to improve the RE Engine piece by piece. This includes the use of AI, which gave fans pause after the news broke online.

We bent the ear of a spokesperson at Capcom, who laid out the challenges its developers are currently facing that led the company to rethink how it makes games with the RE Engine. They confirmed that games are becoming increasingly colossal undertakings, to the point where titles now take up immense amounts of time and resources to create. With AI being a swiftly-advancing technology, Capcom saw the opportunity to use it to solve these issues and make its developers more efficient by improving their development tools, testing game code for them, and analyzing large chunks of data on their behalf, as well as other helpful benefits.

Capcom’s vision for REX is to implement these AI tools and efficiencies into the next iteration of the RE Engine to help the company make games faster with the strongest tools available to it. The spokesperson told us that Capcom has no plans to use generative AI in the creation of its games (which creates content based on a prompt, as opposed to other types of AI that are used to analyze patterns, make predictions, process data, etc.). Any AI used with the RE Engine will be for the express purpose of speeding up processes and helping development teams be more efficient.

This means that AI will not be used for creating assets or programs in games. Capcom said as much back in March during a shareholders’ meeting , where the company was asked how it intends to use artificial intelligence in its products.

“We will not implement assets generated by AI into our games.” Capcom said. “However, we plan to proactively use it as a contributing technology to improve the efficiency and productivity of the game development process. To this end, we are currently exploring ways to implement it in various areas, including graphics, sound and programming."
Upcoming Capcom games include Resident Evil Veronica and Mega Man: Dual Override.

items.title: Cities: Skylines Announced For Switch 2 While Sequel’s Console Ports Are Still MIA
items.summary: Paradox Interactive has announced Cities: Skylines - Expanded Edition, a Nintendo Switch 2 port of Colossal Or

content.v: Paradox Interactive has announced Cities: Skylines - Expanded Edition, a Nintendo Switch 2 port of Colossal Order's hit 2015 city-builder. While it's great to see Cities: Skylines make its way to a new platform, this announcement also serves as a reminder that we have no idea when the long-awaited console ports of Cities: Skylines 2 will come out.

Cities: Skylines - Expanded Edition was developed by Tantalus Media, the team behind The Legend of Zelda: Skyward Sword's Switch port . It'll cost $49, include 10 expansions, expand the buildable area to 25 tiles, support keyboard and mouse, and add a map editor, plus better precision placement and environmental controls. Players can choose between a 30fps mode that focuses on visual quality or a performance mode targeting 60fps.

The Switch 2 port launches on October 28 and will be available at a 70% discount to those who already own the Switch 1 version. Holiday Getaways, Mansions & Manors, and Blueprint Beasts Radio content creator packs will be released for the PC, PS4, and Xbox One versions of the game on the same day.

While the original Cities: Skylines continues to be updated and ported to new platforms, Cities: Skylines 2 and its prospective console ports have had a much rockier journey. That sequel was supposed to be released the same day on PC and console in October 2023, but the console ports were pushed back to Spring 2024 ahead of release. When the PC version of Cities: Skylines 2 launched, it was riddled with bugs and other issues, and developer Colossal Order spent months fixing them.

In Spring 2024, the console ports of Cities: Skylines 2 were delayed again, this time to October 2024. Unfortunately, the PS5 and Xbox Series X|S ports were delayed again, and the developers admitted , "We have not yet met the stability and performance targets we set for the console release." Over two years later, the port is still not out.

In November 2025, Iceflake Studios took over development of Cities: Skylines 2 from Colossal Order, teasing that it will do "continuous work on the Editor and console editions." We have not heard anything about console ports of Cities: Skylines 2 since then.

As Tanatlus Media developed Cities: Skylines - Expanded Edition for Switch 2, not Iceflake Studios, it's unlikely the releases are connected in any significant way. Still, the status of the Cities: Skylines 2 console ports remains a mystery, further complicated by this Switch 2 port announcement and the reveal of Lego Skylines for PC and console.

items.title: WoW: Forever Players Love It When Things Look Old
items.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever players have made their feelings about the game's visual style crystal clear: They

content.v: World of Warcraft: Forever players have made their feelings about the game's visual style crystal clear: They love it when things look old.

It's a recurring theme in the Forever beta, where players have continually pushed back against updated high-definition character models and character portraits. While Forever is in many ways a new version of Blizzard's MMORPG, it's built with the spirit and foundation of WoW Classic in mind, even as it includes updated visuals and quality-of-life updates taken straight from modern WoW. One of those new features is an option to use modern WoW's updated playable character and non-enemy NPC models.

According to the WoW content creator Savix , who tested an early version of Forever before it was publicly announced, developer Blizzard didn't originally plan to include the ability to swap between standard or high-def character models, instead only using HD models. The testers, many of them streamers and content creators from within the WoW Classic community, stressed how important it was to include an option for the game's original character models.

Blizzard thankfully listened, but every other instance of updated character models have been met with similar distaste from among the MMO's community. Whether it was intentional or by mistake, a quilboar boss was found to be using its modern WoW model and was met with backlash from players. It didn't take long for Blizzard to return the enemy back to how it looked in WoW Classic.

It's a similar story with the game's character creation portraits. For much of the beta, the Forever character-creation screen used HD portraits taken from modern WoW, to the disappointment of the community. Earlier this week that finally changed , with the game now using WoW's original character-creation portraits.

Blizzard seems to have gotten the message. Currently, the game's new playable Skyborne elf race only has HD models. That, too, sounds like it will soon change. In a comment attached to a video exploring Skyborne lore and abilities, Blizzard said to "stay tuned regarding Skyborne models," seemingly implying standard-definition versions of the Skyborne are on the way.

Even with these options, some players want more. Forever's user interface is a fascinating combination of old and new--cleaner and more streamlined similar to modern WoW, but inspired in many ways by WoW Classic. Currently, there's not a toggle option to swap between Forever's updated UI and WoW's original interface. For those who want the UI as it was 20 years ago, a player-made ClassicUI Forever add-on reverts many of Blizzard's changes to make everything from the game's action bars, spellbook, profession tab, character portraits, bags, and more look as they did in 2004.

I expect this push and pull to continue. WoW content creators have debated the clash between old and new found in Forever's art style, with many calling on Blizzard to pick a lane. For what seems like the majority of the Forever community, the answer is loud and clear--the older looking the better.

WoW: Forever's beta runs through October 21, with Forever's full launch coming November 4. A recent RMT controversy in the Forever beta saw Blizzard put its foot down when it comes to illegal gold buying . Meanwhile, Blizzard is asking players in a survey for their opinions on 11 potential new classes that could be added to Forever in the future.
